entries.title: Spotify, connected once
notes: !configurespotify connects Spotify for good. Authorization Code with PKCE, so it renews itself in the background and you never paste anything again -- rather than a token that died after an hour.

PKCE means NO client secret. What sits in the config is a refresh token and a client ID; the hub trades them for a fresh access token a minute before each one lapses, and a 401 mid-session renews and retries instead of telling you to reconnect.
Spotify Premium is required, and the setup modal says so first -- for playback control, as always, and since February 2026 to hold a developer app at all.

Every link in setup has a copy button: the dashboard, the exact redirect URI, and the authorise link built from your Client ID. Paste the whole address bar back; the hub finds the code in it, and says 'access denied' rather than 'no code' when you press Cancel.
The setup fields use the same wash, corner and type as everything else in the modal. They were an opaque slab with a stroke that snapped on when focused, which read as a form bolted onto the design.
SHA-256 and base64url in Lua, because Spotify refuses PKCE's plain method. Verified against FIPS 180-4 vectors and RFC 7636's canonical challenge.

The card rests COMPACT: cover, track, artist and 0:42 / 3:14 in a strip. Click it for the four tabs. It shows itself when something starts playing and gets out of the way when nothing is -- closing it by hand is respected until the track changes.
Covers are real images -- fetched, written and served through getcustomasset, capped at 24 with the oldest evicted, cleared on disconnect.
Without opening the card: !play (resume, or search-and-play by name), !pause, !skip, !back, !vol, !np, !unspotify.

Migrated to Spotify's February 2026 API. PUT/DELETE /me/tracks, GET /me/tracks/contains and both /playlists/{id}/tracks endpoints were removed outright -- liking, the heart state, opening a playlist and adding to one all now use /me/library and /playlists/{id}/items. Search's maximum dropped from 50 to 10.
Transport icons from Musicbot's own set, re-cut as outlines to match the hub's stroke weight, plus a mirrored previous and an outline heart for the unliked state.

Now playing is rebuilt: the cover is lifted off the glass with a shadow, the artist is in accent rather than a second grey, transport is bare glyphs that scale and brighten under the cursor and align to the title, and the scrubber runs along the bottom edge. It advances every frame instead of twice a second.
Whichever track is playing is marked in Queue, Search and Lists -- accent title, a rule down the edge, and a glyph that tells playing from paused.
A track change raises a toast with the cover in it, the way a player command shows the target's face.
The card sits above the clock/weather card: what is playing changes more often than the time does.

Fixes from real use: the search magnifier sat after your text because UIPadding moves children as well as text; covers were JPEGs written into .png files, which some executors accept and some silently refuse, so some art rendered and some was a blank tile; one cover shared by several rows only ever reached the first of them; the queue showed the same track eight times; and add-to-playlist could send an empty uri list and come back as 'missing required field uris'.

entries.title: Fling that actually throws people
notes: Fling is rebuilt on the method from Universal Hub MAIN. It goes to them and drives your root through their head on alternating offsets, every frame, carrying a velocity the solver can only resolve by launching somebody. The old one spun you in place and hoped they walked into it.
!fling all works. Fling was never registered as a command that takes a crowd, so the token fell through to a name lookup and answered 'no one matched all' -- while the tips screen advertised it.

You come back. Each throw records where you were standing and returns you there before the next target, so a fling all does not end after one person with you out past the skybox. Stopping mid-throw puts you down too.
A bare !fling still means stand still and fling whoever touches you, which is the only thing the old one was ever good for. Give it a name or 'all' to go and get them.
The kill plane and the seated state are put back on stop, on !stopall, and on unload -- a fling interrupted halfway used to leave the whole game with no kill plane and no UI left to fix it.
Finding nothing is an answer, not a row: a sad face and 'Nothing found' centred in the drawer, at a size you can read, for a misspelt command as well as an empty search.
Scripts already running are greyed in the command bar with a badge, so you can see it before you press rather than after the bar has closed.
Picking a script no longer also runs what you typed as a command.
Three new player tokens, on every command that can take them: nearby (everyone within 100 studs), friends (everyone here off your friends list), and joined (whoever arrived last).

fling all no longer misses people. A throw that failed because they were respawning or had not loaded is retried instead of skipped, nobody is thrown twice, and dying halfway no longer ends the run -- it waits for you to come back and carries on.
Flinging someone already flung this run warns instead of restarting the whole job and abandoning everyone still queued.
A crowd token that names nobody says which one was empty -- 'No one is nearby', not 'no one matched nearby', which reads like a typo.
Fling's notification carries the target's headshot, like every other player command already did.
Fling takes a fourth word: seconds on each target, hinted in the bar like every other valued command. !fling all fly 4.

!sfling is its own command now. Standing still and flinging whoever touches you was a fling TYPE, which it never was -- it has no target, so a player, a crowd token and seconds each all meant nothing for it.
The suggestion list shows every token. It used to keep two while nothing was typed, which hid five of the seven behind already knowing the word.

!introvert (or !hermit, !antisocial, !avoidfriends) leaves the game the moment someone on your friends list joins. !extrovert turns it off, and so does unloading or !stopall -- it is the only thing here that acts on its own, so it cannot be left armed behind you.

Tokens no longer look like players in the suggestion list. Their tile was a circle -- which at that size is what a headshot is -- so a block of them read as a block of people wearing glyphs. Squared off, with a rule under the last one.

entries.title: Mobile, animation packs, and a bar that moves
notes: The bar drags anywhere and remembers where. Cards open downward, or upward when there is no room below.
Dragging has weight everywhere -- the bar, the activity panel and the script hub ease toward the pointer instead of welding to it.
Every card fits the screen it is on. Modals scale to the viewport, drawers to the room actually below them.
Touch: a labelled Commands pill that rides the card stack, tap-away to close the bar, and fly steers from the thumbstick.
Animation packs replicate -- the locomotion is driven through the Animator rather than by editing the Animate script, which only ever changed what you saw.
23 animation packs, resolved to their real animation ids. Twelve executor logos in Info.
vfly, fling, copy, walkto, follow, animpack, clearworkspace, fixanim, rexec.
Fetches carry a cache-buster, so a re-execute gets the newest build instead of the CDN's five-minute-old copy.
The camera's field of view is restored to whatever the game had, not a hardcoded 70.
Search ScriptBlox straight from the command bar: star a result, or open the hub already searched for it. Scripts never displace a command -- typing copy gets you the copy command.
!changelog, and a version that only moves when there is an entry explaining what moved with it.
The hub does not drag -- neither the bar nor the command bar. The floating panels (activity, script hub) still do, as they always have.
Command bar search shows a sweeping bar while it waits on ScriptBlox, and an empty bar offers the scripts you ran most recently -- from the hub or from the bar, same list.
Strings are encrypted now, not just locals renamed -- the published file has no readable text in it at all.
Script hub gains Running and Last used tabs; Last used follows you between games rather than resetting per place.
Command bar: searches the whole line, shows recents and scripts for this game, marks verified and key-locked ones, and says so when there are no results.

Every shipped asset is renamed uhub_*. The executor resolves getcustomasset by FILENAME, not by path, so three scripts each shipping a logo.png fought over the name -- which is why Infinite Yield wore our mark and our splash wore another hub's bird.

entries.title: LITE V2 -- rebuilt, not updated
notes: V2 is not V1 with features bolted on. The interface, the command pipeline and the storage were all rewritten.
One glass design system: every bar, chip, card and modal is built from the same treatment, so the whole thing reads as one product rather than a pile of scripts.
A real command bar -- ranked suggestions, player and mode tokens with aliases, argument hints, and Enter that knows whether to complete or run.
Cards instead of windows: clock, weather, performance, profile and settings all live in one stack that reflows around whatever is open.
Everything persists -- theme, prefix, keybind, favourites, positions, usage -- and survives a teleport.
Ships from GitHub with its own icons and font, downloaded once on first run.
Infinite Yield's command set imported wholesale, so V2 is a superset of what V1 could do.
